This extensive journey through three South American countries links Santiago de Chile, high-altitude deserts and the Uyuni Salt Flat, Torres del Paine, a cruise through the fjords of southern Patagonia and Tierra del Fuego, Ushuaia, Buenos Aires and Bariloche. Over 18 days the scenery changes dramatically several times. Major cities give way to the lagoons and volcanoes of the Altiplano, followed by the glaciers, straits and forests of Patagonia. The tour ends among Argentina’s lakes and mountains.

## Trip highlights

The itinerary starts in Santiago, Chile, and continues through the Atacama Desert to the Bolivian border. Spend several days traveling by 4x4 past Laguna Verde, the Salvador Dalí Desert, the Sol de Mañana geysers, Laguna Colorada and the Uyuni Salt Flat.

The next part of the trip explores Patagonia. Visit Torres del Paine from Puerto Natales, then board the cruise in Punta Arenas and sail through the Strait of Magellan and the Beagle Channel. Stops include Ainsworth Bay, the Tucker Islets, Pia Glacier, Glacier Alley and Wulaia Bay, with a landing at Cape Horn if the weather permits.

After the cruise, the itinerary continues in Ushuaia and Tierra del Fuego National Park. Then celebrate the New Year in Buenos Aires with a tango show, city sightseeing and culinary experiences.

The final part of the trip takes place in Bariloche and includes the Small Circuit, Lake Nahuel Huapi, Victoria Island and myrtle forests.

## How the trip is organized

The journey involves several flights and marked changes in altitude and landscape. In the first few days, travel from the capital city of Santiago to the Bolivian highlands, where the route crosses deserts, passes lagoons and traverses the Uyuni Salt Flat by 4x4. Then return to Chile and fly south to Patagonia.

The Patagonian leg has two parts. First comes a land excursion to Torres del Paine, followed by a four-day voyage from Punta Arenas to Ushuaia. The cruise includes Zodiac landings and hikes of varying difficulty. Some landings depend on the weather, so their order and whether they can go ahead may change.

After the rugged landscapes of Tierra del Fuego, the trip continues in the city. Spend several days exploring the tango, architecture and food of Buenos Aires. Then return to nature in Bariloche, where catamaran outings complement the lakes, mountains and forests.

The trip runs from 20 December to 6 January. New Year’s Eve is spent in Buenos Aires. Accommodation, the cruise and the specific hotels are tied to these dates, so moving any of the days would require the logistics to be worked out again.

## Altitude and seasonal conditions

The high-altitude part of the route begins in Bolivia. The Uyuni Salt Flat is approximately 3,650 m above sea level. In the dry season it looks like an unbroken white salt plain. During the rains, a thin layer of water turns it into a vast mirror. The same route therefore looks markedly different depending on the season.

The cruise itinerary also varies seasonally. Magellanic penguins may be absent from the Tucker Islets in September and April. In that case, the landing is replaced by a walk to the glacier in Brooks Bay. Landing at Cape Horn depends on the weather and sea conditions in every season.

## Cruise details

The cruise runs from 26 to 30 December in a category AA cabin.

Small Zodiac boats are used for landings in bays and at the islands.

The walks vary in difficulty. At Ainsworth Bay, choose between a gentler walk through the subpolar forest and a more demanding route along the moraine. At Pia Glacier, there is also a standard walk and a more challenging hike along the lateral moraine.

Weather directly affects the itinerary. Cape Horn is accessible only when sea conditions are safe. If a landing is impossible, the cruise continues at the discretion of the captain and crew.

Seasonal conditions also matter at the Tucker Islets. In September and April, the Magellanic penguins are elsewhere, so a walk to Brooks Glacier replaces penguin watching.

The cruise passes through places with a rich maritime history, including the Strait of Magellan, the Beagle Channel, Wulaia Bay and Cape Horn. This part of the trip combines glaciers and wildlife with the history of exploration at the continent’s southern tip.
